item.title: How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins
item.description: How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Like many multi-million and billion-dollar entities, the Penguins have postured themselves as a family for the better part of six decades. Their history suggests that label isn't entirely inaccurate. Pittsburgh's roster has housed an impressive number of brother pairings, from Doug and Greg Brown and Chris and Peter Ferraro to Mario and Alain Lemieux (for one game). For a fleeting moment during the offseason, it appeared that they might have added another. After landing Nick Robertson in a trade with the Maple Leafs, the Penguins turned their sights to his high-profile brother, Jason Robertson. Those plans didn't quite come to fruition. But all hope is not lost just yet. With that, here's what you need to know about Pittsburgh's pursuit of Jason Robertson — aided in no small part by its decision to acquire his younger brother, Nick. MORE: Jaromir Jagr Teases Career Decision After 38th Professional Season How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins The elder Robertson was linked heavily with Pittsburgh in the offseason. The Stars standout commanded significant interest from the Penguins, with general manager Kyle Dubas believed to have attempted to lodge a trade offer at Dallas, according to The Athletic's Josh Yohe. Pittsburgh's acquisition of the younger Robertson via trade with the Maple Leafs figured to improve its bargaining position. The Stars were known to be in talks with teams over a potential swap for Jason, who hit restricted free agency after the 2025-26 season ended. They even agreed to a deal with the Kraken that would have sent the No. 7 pick and assets to Dallas in exchange for Jason Robertson. However, the deal was nixed at the 11th hour after Jason refused signing a long-term extension to stay in Seattle. Jason would eventually ink a one-year, $12 million deal to stay with the Stars for the 2026-27 season. Dallas has been known to covet agreeing terms to a longer-term deal with the winger, who has produced 516 points in 478 games. The Stars offered him a qualifying offer prior to the start of free agency. If they opted against matching a bid on him by other teams, they would have secured draft-pick compensation — four first-round selections for a player of Robertson's projected value. His contractual situation — Robertson will hit unrestricted free agency at the end of the season, meaning Dallas stands to lose him for nothing if he decides to go elsewhere — could force the Stars to deal him at the trade deadline if they feel he's leaning towards leaving the team at the end of the year. Nick's arrival could improve Pittsburgh's chances of attracting Jason, one of the sport's most dynamic forwards. Any movement involving Jason Robertson will take place in the new year. Dallas can't offer Jason an extension until next January,

item.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
item.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. That's where an eclipse almost 1,300 years later becomes particularly intriguing. Is the oldest recorded eclipse hidden in the Bible? Researchers have proposed that an annular eclipse occurred over Canaan on Oct. 30, 1207 BC, and may be described in the Bible. This image was captured during an annular solar eclipse from Redding, California on May 20, 2012. (Image credit: Paul Souders via Getty Images) A passage in the Old Testament book of Joshua describes the sun and moon as if they stopped in the sky. After leading the people of Israel into Canaan — modern-day Israel and Palestine — Joshua prayed: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on their enemies." Ancient Gibeon is about six miles (10 kilometers) northwest of Jerusalem. In research published in 2017, researchers Colin Humphreys and Graeme Waddington at Cambridge University in the U.K. claimed it could refer to an annular solar eclipse on Oct. 30, 1207 B.C. It's a controversial interpretation, not least because it depends on exactly how the ancient Hebrew text is translated. However, if correct, it could be t

item.title: Napoli Interested in Sassuolo Loanee and Young Goalie
item.description: Napoli Interested in Sassuolo Loanee and Young Goalie Napoli have recently rekindled interest in Sebastiano Esposito, whom they tracked extensively last summer before Sassuolo snapped him up late after he had a falling out with Cagliari. The Azzurri settled for giving Lorenzo Lucca and Noa Lang another chance after their loan spells. According to Alfredo Pedullà , the Neroverdi beat Torino and Genoa in the race, bringing the striker in temporarily with a €1M fee and a €11M option to buy. If the Partenopei offloaded their misfits, he’d be among their top targets to replenish their attack thanks to his versatility. Sassuolo aren’t in good shape in the standings and would like to keep Esposito, so Napoli would have to table a very persuasive offer, Corriere dello Sport relays. In addition to searching for new weapons, their director Giovanni Manna recently met with the entourage of Coritiba goalie Pedro Morisco. The Azzurri could accelerate their plans to add a new shot-stopper. Alex Meret just suffered a fifth vertebra fracture that will sideline him for at least two months. Moreover, his contract is up at the end of the season, and Vanja Milinkovic-Savic hasn’t been entirely convincing. The 22-year-old represented the national team twice with Carlo Ancelotti at the helm. He has kept 44 clean sheets and conceded 107 goals in 113 matches with his club. Our Take on Napoli, Esposito, and Morisco It’s not great that they’re linked to other attackers shortly after meeting with Gustavo Varela’s agent , although they’re pretty different, and the Sassuolo man would pair up better with Rasmus Hojlund. The deal is technically difficult but not impossible if they are willing to spend. At some point, they’ll have to choose between the sticks, and the answer might not be one of their current options.

item.title: Iga Swiatek tipped to be a real ‘dark horse’ on the WTA Tour in 2027 by Serena Williams’ ex-coach
item.description: Iga Swiatek will want to get back to competing for Grand Slams once again in 2027 after a largely disappointing 2026 season. Though there were some high points, most notably her triumph at the Canadian Open, this season was a difficult one for Swiatek , who had won at least one Grand Slam each year from 2022 to 2025. That streak came to an end this year, with the Pole reaching just one major quarterfinal at the Australian Open before bowing out of Roland Garros, Wimbledon and the US Open early. Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images Rick Macci previews Iga Swiatek’s 2027 season on the WTA Tour Swiatek has confirmed her first tournament of the 2027 season will be the Brisbane International, and Serena Williams’ former coach, Rick Macci, has high expectations for the 25-year-old ahead of her trip to Australia. In a post on X , formerly known as Twitter, Macci said: “The Polish Punisher is my dark horse in 2027. With all her current weapons (speed, quickness angles fight grit proven and groovin) and even if her effective but limited serve stays the same(hope not) the wildcard for the Punisher is what happens After each point between her ears will determine if Iga finds a few more gears.” In another post, Macci said: “Iga should go into the lab and experiment like never before. Off the ground she is ok and sound. Just discussions on certain moments in combat as most coaches have said that. If her mindset is steady and loving the battle the Punisher is hard to rattle. “But in the off-season, everything is on the table with the serve and see if they can rewire and change a nerve. Experiment with grip stance takeback pinpoint platform power position ball toss hip and elbow angles to get more easy power and location but her legs have to drive the racquet IN at the proper time to get the optimal external and internal shoulder rotation.” Swiatek finished the 2026 season ranked ninth in the world, having started the year second.

item.title: Bournemouth is now ready to sell Arsenal target in the new year
item.description: Bournemouth is now ready to sell Arsenal target in the new year Alex Scott has become one of the most sought-after players in Europe following his impressive form for Bournemouth over the last few campaigns. The midfielder has continued to develop during his time with the Cherries, attracting attention from clubs looking to strengthen their squads with young English talent. Bournemouth would be keen to keep hold of him as they continue to make progress as a team. Scott has also been working hard to improve, and his performances have made him an important player for the club. However, keeping him may prove difficult as interest in his services continues to grow. Arsenal could have an opportunity to sign Scott The Cherries have offered the midfielder a new contract in an attempt to secure his future, but he has continued to turn down their proposals . Scott is understood to be keen on moving to a much bigger club, leaving Bournemouth facing an increasingly difficult situation as they consider how best to handle his future. Arsenal are among the clubs interested in signing him, and the latest development could give the Gunners encouragement in their pursuit. The midfielder’s desire to take the next step in his career could make a departure increasingly likely, particularly if Bournemouth decide that keeping him is no longer realistic. The Gunners will be aware that they are unlikely to be alone in the race. Scott’s form has attracted wider attention, and the possibility of him becoming available could encourage other interested sides to make their intentions clear. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Bournemouth could consider a January sale According to Team Talk , Bournemouth have given up on trying to keep Scott and now believe that selling him in January could be the smartest option. The report says the club see the winter window as an opportunity to secure a substantial fee for the midfielder’s signature. A decision to make him available in two months would put several clubs on alert and could lead to increased competition for his services. Bournemouth would have the chance to attract offers from teams prepared to pay a significant amount to bring him in. If Arsenal are serious about signing the England star, they will need to be ready to meet Bournemouth’s valuation. The Gunners may have an opportunity to strengthen their squad, but competition for Scott could make the deal expensive, especially if several clubs decide to pursue him in January. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Season-Ending News for Puka Nacua Fantasy Football Managers as Davante Adams and Konata Mumpfield Get a Value Boost
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) reacts after making a touchdown catch in the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Puka Nacua MCL Surgery: Fantasy Football Fallout for the Rams Offense Fantasy football managers holding onto hope for a late-season return from Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua just received devastating news. According to reports, Nacua has undergone surgery on his injured MCL. Rams head coach Sean McVay confirmed the procedure on Friday, stating that the standout pass-catcher will be sidelined for "a couple of months", a timeline that effectively puts his regular season on ice and leaves fantasy managers scrambling ahead of Week 12. Rams standout WR Puka Nacua is undergoing surgery on his MCL surgery and now could miss the rest of the season. Rams HC Sean McVay confirmed the surgery while saying Nacua will be out "a couple of months." pic.twitter.com/mG572hwkWA - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 20, 2026 With Los Angeles sitting at 6-4 coming out of their Week 11 bye and preparing to host the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25, the ripple effects across the Rams' depth chart are massive. Let's look at how to handle Nacua on your fantasy roster and dig into which Los Angeles playmakers stand to benefit most down the stretch. Is Puka Nacua Droppable in Fantasy Football? Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) stiff arms Washington Commanders cornerback Trey Amos (23) during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you play in a standard redraft or single-season league, the answer is straightforward: yes, you can safely drop Puka Nacua. Even before this surgical update, Nacua was already dealing with a knee sprain suffered in Week 9 against Washington alongside a three-game suspension . Now, a "couple of months" recovery timeline puts his earliest realistic return around mid-to-late January (well after the NFL regular season concludes and long after fantasy championships are decided in Week 17). Unless you are in a dynasty or keeper format where you can comfortably stash him on an Injured Reserve spot for 2027, there is no reason to let Nacua clog up a valuable bench slot during the fantasy playoff push. item.title: Tom Brady calls out NFL players for extravagant touchdown celebrations
item.description: Former NFL quarterback Tom Brady is taking aim at today’s players, criticizing the elaborate touchdown celebrations that have become increasingly popular across the league. During a recent appearance on Fox Sports’ weekly ‘ Ask Tom ‘ segment, the seven-time Super Bowl champion shared his frustration with the amount of choreography players put into their end zone celebrations. “I’ve seen more choreography in some of these touchdown celebrations than in a Broadway show, learn your assignments, how about that,” Brady said. A little more playbook, a little less Broadway, if you ask @TomBrady. https://t.co/HCj7BQz5h2 — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 20, 2026 The legendary quarterback specifically referenced the Detroit Lions’ controversial celebration during their international game in Munich, Germany, which quickly became a talking point around the league. Brady questioned how players can remember elaborate routines while occasionally struggling with fundamental responsibilities on the field. MORE: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 11 Brady takes aim at Lions’ controversial celebration Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the New England Patriots in the second half of the 2026 NFL Munich Game at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Brady recalled playing alongside teammates who struggled to remember their third-down assignments, blocked the wrong defenders during running plays or committed costly offsides penalties. He then jokingly questioned how those same types of players could suddenly remember an elaborate routine. “Guys that couldn’t remember their third down assignments, that blocked the wrong people in the run game, that jumped offside,” Brady said, before expressing his amusement that players could remember “a 12-person choreographed centipede celebration.” The Lions’ centipede celebration in Munich generated plenty of reactions from around the NFL, with several people expressing their displeasure with the unusual routine. However, Detroit’s players clearly enjoyed the moment, and the celebration was something they had planned after getting inspiration from an unexpected source. MORE: Predicting upsets in Week 11 on NFL season Amon-Ra St. Brown reveals celebration inspiration Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) celebrates with a german flag after the Lions defeated the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who scored the touchdown that sparked the memorable celebration, explained how the idea originally came together. According to St. Brown, one of the team’s coaches introduced the concept during a meeting. “We had a meeting… coach [Mike] Kafka comes up. item.title: Over 12 Teams Reportedly Trying To Sign Freddy Peralta; Cubs, Padres, Rays Included
item.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta Freddy Peralta is one of the best players available in free agency this year, and while all of the headlines are about Tarik Skubal, Peralta is reportedly drawing plenty of interest. There are still over a half a dozen teams in play for Peralta with the Padres, both Chicago teams and believe it or not the Rays all still involved and maybe the Braves too but the latter not confirmed," wrote MLB insider Jim Bowden on X on Friday. "Other teams are in the periphery but not as aggressive. It's getting late and time for teams to pick it up or lose out." Peralta is a two-time All-Star who had an up-and-down season. He struggled with the New York Mets, but thrived with the Tampa Bay Rays after the trade deadline. On the Rays, he had a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular season starts, posting a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular season starts. In the postseason, he logged a 1.08 ERA through his first four outings and was even named the American League Championship Series MVP. His final postseason start came against the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series and he allowed five runs in 4 2/3 innings of work. Peralta was a great pitcher for the Brewers in the first eight seasons of his career. He lost his way in Queens, but the Rays helped him find himself again. He is set up for a nine-figure payday as a free agent, but may have to wait for Skubal to sign to get his best offers. More MLB: This Red Sox Trade Idea Would Swap Curtis Mead, Jarren Duran For Three-Time All-Star

item.title: Infantino inspects Warri Stadium, pledges FIFA support during visit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the remodeled Warri City Stadium and pledged the world football body’s continued support for Nigerian football. Infantino visited the Delta State facility on Friday with FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, ahead of its scheduled commissioning on Saturday. He was received at Osubi Airport by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria Football Federation president Amaju Pinnick. Infantino praised the Delta State Government’s investment, saying modern sports facilities could help develop young talent and expand opportunities for boys and girls. He also celebrated Nigeria’s football heritage, highlighting the country’s contribution to the global game. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball,” he said, adding that he hoped to return and play there once the remaining work was completed. The FIFA president also congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, on winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing their triumph as a source of pride. “You will always count on FIFA and on the FIFA president as your not just partner, but your family member,” Infantino said. Oborevwori said the inspection was an opportunity to assess the stadium’s readiness against international standards. In a post on X, the governor described the renovation as extensive and said the state remained committed to delivering world-class sports infrastructure. He wrote: “It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning. We thereafter proceeded to the Warri Stadium, where we inspected the facility to assess its readiness against international standards,” “The transformation is extensive, and our commitment remains to deliver world-class sporting infrastructure that will position Delta State to compete on the global stage and emerge as a hub for sporting excellence. In the words of the FIFA President, Gianni Infantino: “This is fantastic!” It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning. We thereafter proceeded to the Warri Stadium, where we inspected the facility to assess its readiness against international standards. item.title: U15s face Santos at Vila Belmiro in Paulista semi-final second leg
item.description: U15s face Santos at Vila Belmiro in Paulista semi-final second leg This Saturday, the Under-15s face Santos at 9 a.m. at Vila Belmiro in Santos, São Paulo, in the second leg of the Campeonato Paulista semifinals for their age group. Led by coach Vinícius dos Santos, the team has put together a solid Campeonato Paulista campaign. They finished top of their group in both of the first two stages, recording 14 wins, three draws and just one defeat, with 68 goals scored and ten conceded. As the competition progressed, the Tricolor got past AA Flamengo in the third stage after a 1-1 away draw and a 3-0 win in Cotia. In the round of 16, they eliminated Guarani with a 5-0 home rout and a 1-1 draw in Campinas. In the quarterfinals, they overcame Palmeiras: after drawing the first leg 2-2, they came from behind to win 2-1 at Arena Crefisa Barueri. In the first leg of the semifinals, played at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, the Tricolor beat Santos 1-0 thanks to a goal from Enzo Henrique. With that advantage, the team need only a draw in the return leg at Vila Belmiro to secure a place in the state championship final. A defeat by a one-goal margin would send the tie to a penalty shootout. So far, they have played 25 matches, with 18 wins, six draws and just one defeat. They have scored 83 goals and conceded 14. Under-14s In the afternoon, the Under-14s return to action against Guarani at 2:30 p.m. at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, São Paulo, for the second leg of the Campeonato Paulista semifinal. In the first leg, played last Sunday at Estádio Brinco de Ouro da Princesa in Campinas, São Paulo, the Tricolor won 2-0 with goals from center-backs Guilherme Barbosa and Estevão, taking the lead in the battle for a place in the final. Credits: Victor Wajnsztejn / São Paulo FC This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Wife of Newly-Traded Ravens Player Shares Lengthy Apology After Backlash for Calling Baltimore ‘Scary’
item.description: Allie and Ryan Neuzil via Instagram Credit: Allie Neuzil/Instagram NEED TO KNOW The wife of newly-traded Ravens player Ryan Neuzil apologized for calling the city “scary” “People were offended by this, so there’s no question about it, no ifs and buts,” she said The incident comes in the same week that Ravens benched Marlon Humphrey for insensitive comments about the city The wife of a newly-traded Baltimore Ravens player issued a lengthy apology after she called the city “scary” in a since-deleted TikTok. Allie Neuzil, whose husband Ryan Neuzil was traded to the Ravens at the NFL’s trade deadline last week, said she is “so sorry for what was said and for offending people” in an apology video on TikTok on Thursday, Nov. 19. In addition to calling the city of Baltimore “scary” in her video, Allie drew backlash because she filmed a Baltimore resident who appeared to be in active addiction. “People were offended by this, so there’s no question about it, no ifs and buts,” Allie said, noting that she didn’t want to “repost the video because obviously it wasn’t received well.” Allie said that she hadn’t been to Baltimore yet at the time of her posting the video, and she had only “heard things” and “received warnings from people” about the city that influenced her claims. Allie and Ryan Neuzil via Instagram Credit: Allie Neuzil/Instagram “Now that I’ve been in Baltimore, it’s great here,” Allie said, explaining that “part of why” she issued the apology video is because she’s seen that the people of Baltimore are “the nicest people ever” since moving to the city. Addressing the clip of a person experiencing the symptoms of drug use, Allie said it was related to “an inside joke” with her “Atlanta girls” and she thought it could serve as “a callback to my time in Atlanta.” Allie said it was “not my intention to make anything about race” and that she has “a lot of people commenting and calling me racist.” “I literally said so many positive things about coming here and being on the Ravens and how the experience with the Ravens is different from the Falcons and like things that are better here than it was in Atlanta,” she said. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! In another apology on TikTok, Allie addressed the incident involving Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey, who was deactivated for their Week 11 game after making an insensitive joke about Baltimore on his podcast. Humphrey, 30, said the city is “best at making criminals,” which head coach Jesse Minter said is “not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate” on Nov. 19. Minter decided to bench Humphrey for the Ravens’ game on Sunday. item.title: AC Milan eyeing up cut-price swoop for Stuttgart marksman Demirović
item.description: AC Milan eyeing up cut-price swoop for Stuttgart marksman Demirović According to Tuttosport, AC Milan's search for a new goalscorer has now brought Ermedin Demirović into focus. The report states that the Italians see the 28-year-old VfB Stuttgart forward as a far cheaper alternative for the striker position. Other options like Endrick of Real Madrid and Club Brugge star Nicolò Tresoldi would likely cost around €70million each. Adding to the fact that Demirović's contract with Stuttgart expires in 2028, there are currently no signs of an imminent extension. Naturally, that gives those in charge at the Rossoneri reason to be optimistic about negotiating a good deal for the Bosnian. Furthermore, Markus Krösche's excellent connections in the Bundesliga could also help to bring Demirović to the fashion capital. Krösche has reportedly had Demirović on his radar for years. Now he could finally sign the prolific striker. However, Demirović is also on the radar of Premier League clubs and almost joined Turkish giants Galatasaray last summer.

item.title: Chelsea fined £150,000 for discriminatory chanting
item.description: [Getty Images] Chelsea have been fined £150,000 by the Football Association as part of a punishment for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chants during an FA Cup third-round win at Charlton Athletic in January. The club have also been warned about their future conduct and had an action plan imposed on them in relation to the offence. "Chelsea FC failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief," said an FA statement. Chelsea admitted the charge but had an appeal against the fine issued by an independent regulatory commission rejected. The FA's written reasons stated that although the discriminatory chanting "lasted approximately one minute and was not repeated, the scale of participation was a significant aggravating feature". "We unequivocally condemn this behaviour," said a Chelsea statement. "Sectarian abuse - chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group - and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club. "Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary." The FA itself was fined by Uefa for a similar incident of chanting, from England's away support during their Nations League victory in Spain on Sunday. We are experiencing massive contrasts in our performances this season, with our European and League Cup campaigns moving forward dynamically, but we are hiccupping in the most important endeavour for our beloved football club: the Premier League. Competing in the best league in the world brings status, remarkable income and the chance of European competition, for which we qualified so dynamically at the end of last season. Our presence in the top division, without a recurring threat of relegation, makes player recruitment so much easier. Our last home game, with a welcome 1-0 victory over Chelsea, was a real fillip – an exceptional result in what has been quite a drab league season so far. We are all obviously hoping it is a turning point, leading Sunderland to rise up the table. I am really feeling that we have become the West Londoners’ bogey team via Brian Brobbey. The 2-1 win there 13 months ago, with the remarkable late goal from Chemsidine Talbi, was an iconic statement from this team, and when we completed the double late last May, it led us to the promised land of European football. We know, though, that losing becomes a habit and, despite the progress elsewhere, we have been in a rut in the league, especially away from home. There have been many reasons for this: some injuries which dragged on long after the World Cup and other international games. We missed our main strikers, Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, early on and, although Timur Tutierov has emerged, this has been tough for the team and is reflected in match outcomes. Dan Ballard has been a miss, but several players have just looked off colour, such as Omar Aldrete. item.title: The Chicago Bears Can’t Afford To Overlook the Saints
item.description: The Chicago Bears have spent the first half of the season proving they belong among the NFC’s contenders. Now, coming out of their bye week with a 7-2 record and four consecutive victories, Chicago faces a different challenge: avoiding a setback against an opponent it is expected to beat. The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday’s matchup at Soldier Field with a 3-6 record, but their struggles shouldn’t give Chicago a reason to relax. With a Thanksgiving showdown against the Detroit Lions approaching, the Bears have an opportunity to build momentum before entering one of the most demanding stretches of their season. Chicago has shown it can survive mistakes, but Sunday’s matchup offers a chance to demonstrate something equally important. The Bears need to show they can control a game without relying on another dramatic finish. Ben Johnson on the NFC North Competition: "Doesn't matter right now. Once again, it's all about winning this week, so we'll worry about everything else when it's time. It's not time for that. There's still eight games to be played, and this is the most important one because it's… pic.twitter.com/OdTp4fKYSB — Bears on Real (@BearsOnReal) November 18, 2026 Caleb Williams Must Protect the Football The Bears’ 27-24 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before their bye week was encouraging for the final result, but concerning for the performance that preceded it. Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions, repeatedly giving Tampa Bay opportunities to erase Chicago’s early advantage. Those interceptions weren’t all the result of the same problem. According to the Chicago Sun-Times , Williams acknowledged forcing his first interception toward Rome Odunze in the end zone. Tampa Bay’s pressure contributed to two more poor decisions, while his fourth interception came on a pass tipped at the line of scrimmage. The distinction matters because New Orleans possesses a defensive front capable of creating similar problems. Chase Young and Carl Granderson have combined for 16.5 sacks, giving the Saints two dangerous edge rushers who can disrupt Williams’ timing and force him outside the pocket. Williams cannot afford to let pressure dictate his decision-making. Throwing the football away when a play breaks down and taking available underneath completions would let Chicago maintain possession rather than give New Orleans more opportunities. Despite the turnovers, Williams remains confident in his approach. “I’m going to keep gripping it and keep ripping it,” Williams told reporters following the Tampa Bay victory. That confidence is important, but Chicago needs better decisions to go with it. The Saints have recorded just four interceptions this season, presenting Williams with an opportunity to rebound against a secondary that has struggled to generate takeaways. item.title: Hawks Hits: Costly Slow Start, But Offense Was Capable Without Bedard
item.description: For the fifth time in seven games without captain Connor Bedard this season, the Chicago Blackhawks offense failed to reach three goals in Thursday’s 4-2 loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets . The Blackhawks couldn’t claw their way back from an early 2-0 deficit, with a slow start proving costly in the team’s lone regulation loss of the four-game homestand, finishing 2-1-1. Facing a Columbus team that entered the United Center on the back of five straight losses, with only eight goals during that stretch, it was particularly disappointing that the Hawks were giving up the better chances and losing most of the puck battles and foot races in the early going. The Blue Jackets led 17-7 in shots on goal in the first period and were ahead 22-10 at the game’s midway point, with Cam Talbot not having to do much to maintain the two-goal lead, which the Blackhawks could never overcome. “After a couple good games here, coming up against a team that we know we should beat, giving them the edge to win that game, that’s the difference-maker.” Frank Nazar said after the game. Head coach Jeff Blashill was “extremely” frustrated with the lack of compete, urgency, and execution in the first half, three things he and his players always talk about in the locker room in between periods. “For me, it was not good enough, not good enough, not good enough,” Blashill said, referencing the three aspects. “So then, don’t even talk about X’s and O’s at that point. We weren’t skating. We’re a pressure team. If you don’t skate, you’re a step behind all over the ice. I thought we were really soft with the puck in our own end… and I thought our execution was poor.” After carving his team a bit, Blashill ended that statement by crediting them for not going down without a fight and improving their play over the second half. Over the final 30 minutes, the offense started figuring out how to generate scoring chances without their star player. Despite Bedard’s absence, the power play converted for the fourth straight game, with Frank Nazar netting his team-leading 11th goal of the season in the second period. Still trailing by two entering the third, the Blackhawks were pressing hard and cut the deficit to one again with a snipe from Cole Smith with 16:08 remaining. But even though several players had quality looks to even the score, the equalizer never came, with Talbot hanging tough to keep the Jackets ahead. The Blackhawks outchanced Columbus 10-2 in the finale frame, as Roman Kantserov, Ryan Donato , Ryan Greene, Tyler Bertuzzi , Sam Rinzel , and Nazar each had an opportunity for the game-tying tally. The compete, urgency, and execution was much better in the latter stages, but it was too little too late. “I thought the second and third were much better. We certainly pressured hard, were on top of them, and created chances. But when you dig yourselves a hole in this league, it’s hard. It’s an every-night league, and it’s an every-period league. You can’t have only two of three perio

item.title: Mikel Arteta sends message to Arsenal board over next contract deal
item.description: Mikel Arteta sends message to Arsenal board over next contract deal Arsenal Want Martin Odegaard Contract Sorted as Arteta Makes His Position Clear Arsenal are moving methodically on contracts and the next obvious file on the desk is Martin Odegaard. Mikel Arteta has said it plainly enough. He wants his captain tied down for the long term, because in his view this is not a marginal player or a symbolic armband holder. This is one of the central pieces. The club have already pushed ahead with fresh agreements for key members of their Premier League-winning squad. Declan Rice, David Raya and Jurrien Timber are understood to have agreed terms in recent weeks, while Piero Hincapie has also landed an improved deal. Add that to earlier commitments from Bukayo Saka, William Saliba and Arteta himself, and the strategy is clear. Arsenal are trying to lock in stability before uncertainty has a chance to develop. Arteta sees Odegaard as critical Odegaard’s current contract runs until 2028, but he is edging towards the final 18 months. In modern football that matters. Leave it too long and the conversation changes. It stops being about control and starts being about leverage. Arteta has no interest in ambiguity here. “Martin is an instrumental player for us, for me,” Arteta said. He then expanded on why. “I think what he’s done for the club and for the team in the last years since he joined has just been [on] an uplifted trajectory with some moments of incredible consistency and magic, and some others that are a bit more difficult. Photo IMAGO “But I think his role and my opinion on how important he is to continue to do what we’re doing is critical.” When asked directly whether he wanted Odegaard to remain beyond the current deal, the answer was brief and definitive: “Yes, definitely yes.” Martin Odegaard contract talks still waiting The awkward part is that Odegaard himself said over the international break that talks have not yet started. That stands out when so many team-mates have already progressed or concluded their own negotiations. It does not automatically signal a problem, but it does invite questions. Arteta, predictably, would not open that door. “You know that I never talk about these things,” Arteta said. “I can tell you the opinion I have and I think that’s a very general and unanimous feeling that we have, everyone at the club.” That is standard manager language, but the message underneath it is obvious enough. Arsenal value Odegaard highly and want the situation resolved. Arsenal captain back at his best The timing makes sense. Odegaard looks closer to his proper level again. He has three goals in his first 10 Premier League matches this season after managing only one league goal last term, a season disrupted by shoulder and knee injuries. For an attacking midfielder whose game depends on rhythm, sharpness and repetition, that sort of interruption can derail a campaign quickly. item.title: 'Right time' for Smith exit - but Murray not ready for role
item.description: Leon Smith was Andy Murray's childhood coach before taking over as Britain's Davis Cup captain in 2010 [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" to leave the role after almost 17 years - although Andy Murray is not ready to replace him. Smith was appointed in 2010 and guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this stage. Since retiring in 2024, Murray has been enjoying spending more time with his family and working on business interests, as well as coaching Novak Djokovic and now Jack Draper on a part-time basis. "He obviously is the standout candidate, isn't he?" said Smith. "I do hope it's something he does in the future, but I respect that it's not for him right now, and I can understand it. "But I really hope at some point in the future that he does take it on." Smith said he had been pondering his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna. "There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters. Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] "I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role. "I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray, 39, was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." Smith, who will continue in his role as head of British men's tennis, took over almost 17 years ago with the team in danger of being relegated to the lowest tier of the Davis Cup. Within three years they were back in the top tier and just two years later Murray inspired them to the trophy. Smith also guided the team to the semi-finals in

item.title: Kevin De Bruyne: Napoli express desire to keep player in January
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne: Napoli express desire to keep player in January Serie A side Napoli have been facing a real possibility of losing Kevin De Bruyne in January but they are expected to stand firm in a decision to keep him at the Partenopei. Corriere dello Sport report that PSV have tried to make in-roads over a deal for January but Aurelio de Laurentiis issued a firm ‘no’ to their offer. This is mainly because the club do not want to sell in the winter and even Max Allegri sees him as a lynchpin for the side. But that doesn’t rule out a summer exit, though. De Bruyne’s current deal runs out at the end of the campaign and PSV remain in the hunt. They can now decide to reach an agreement for a deal in the summer, having spoken to the Belgian’s entourage extensively. It is believed their initial plan was to execute a summer deal and they simply wanted to assess the idea of bringing it forward. They have now gone back to their initial plan, as they try to determine whether Napoli will hand him an extension or not. Most importantly, they will rely on the player’s wishes to return closer home to seal a deal and hope that this convinces his entourage. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Rams receiver Nacua out two months after knee surgery
item.description: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, left, says Rams receiver Puka Nacua, right, will be sidelined for a couple of months after undergoing left knee surgery (Dustin Satloff) Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent right knee ligament surgery this week and could miss the remainder of the NFL season, Rams coach Sean McVay said on Friday. Nacua will miss "a couple of months" after the operation, McVay said, a timetable that might allow the 25-year-old pass-catcher to return for the playoffs if the Rams (6-4) qualify. On Thursday, Nacua was suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy in an incident last December. Nacua was already set to miss at least the next three games for the Rams after being placed on injured reserve a week ago with knee and toe injuries suffered in a victory over Washington on November 8. Nacua, in his fourth NFL campaign after being taken by the Rams in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, led the league in receptions last season with 129. This season, he made 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games. js/ea

item.title: Cardinals get bad news on Carson Beck’s status for Week 11 amid back injury
item.description: Cardinals get bad news on Carson Beck’s status for Week 11 amid back injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals are not having a good 2026 season, but it's hardly a surprise given where the team is at as a franchise. But part of the issue isn't just the struggles of the roster; it's the injuries this offense has faced. Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jeremiyah Love are all out for an extended period of time. Only Love might be back at some point this season. Carson Beck is throwing to a lackluster supporting cast. But now even he is banged up. After popping up on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, Beck, according to a report from Theo Mackie of AZ Central Sports , is not looking likely to play in Week 11 against the Kansas City Chiefs . Cardinals not likely to have Carson Beck for Week 11 matchup "Carson Beck will not practice today and the Cardinals will 'proceed' as if Josh Johnson will start on Sunday," Mackie reports. "They're not closing the door on Beck, but it seems unlikely that he'll play." Beck went on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, putting his status for Week 11 in doubt. That doubt now appears to be close to a certainty, as the expectation is Beck will be ruled out for the Chiefs game. Arizona will now be down to their fourth quarterback this season, as Jacoby Brissett has been traded to the Baltimore Ravens , Minshew and Beck are hurt, and now Josh Johnson is set to take over. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day The 3-7 Cardinals are going up against the 7-2 Chiefs in Week 11, in what's looking like a near-insurmountable matchup. Down to QB4 on the season with a lackluster supporting cast is far from ideal. While Beck played poorly in his NFL debut, going 11 of 18 passing for 108 yards and two picks with no touchdowns, it's still a big blow to lose Beck for Week 11. He's not yet ruled out, but Cardinals fans should anticipate missing out on Beck for Week 11 against the Chiefs, with a return in Week 12 or Week 13 against the Washington Commanders or Philadelphia Eagles more likely to be Beck's second NFL start. item.title: Maple Leafs Coach Jim Hiller Explains Head-Scratching Gavin McKenna Decision
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 28: Gavin McKenna #92 of the Toronto Maple Leafs looks on during the first period against the Seattle Kraken at Climate Pledge Arena on October 28, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Toronto Maple Leafs rookie Gavin McKenna is clearly still figuring life out in the NHL. But, that being said, he possesses a skill set that very few NHLers seem to have. The 18-year-old phenom is a wizard with the puck on his stick, and he’s shown that early in his NHL career with a quietly impressive six goals and 14 points in 24 games. Even though he’s shown an ability to produce early, Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller seems unwilling to put him in the situation that would best utilize his skill set. Jim Hiller Explains Why Gavin McKenna Isn’t Playing in Overtime The Maple Leafs have gone to overtime three times this season, but McKenna hasn’t played a single shift in the extra frame. That continued Thursday against Los Angeles, when Hiller instead leaned on Auston Matthews, William Nylander, John Tavares, Easton Cowan and Jack Roslovic. Speaking to reporters after the loss, Hiller acknowledged that McKenna’s offensive talent doesn’t necessarily guarantee him an opportunity in three-on-three situations. “I don’t really evaluate his 5-on-5 play into 3-on-3,” Hiller said, via Maple Leafs Hotstove . “3-on-3, it’s just a different game in the NHL.” Jim Hiller on why Gavin Mckenna is yet to play a shift in overtime this season. 🤔 pic.twitter.com/uhdRcjkpEB — BarDown (@BarDown) November 20, 2026 The coach also revealed that McKenna has come close to getting an opportunity, only to be called back to the bench. “He’s watched. We’ve had him up and then called him off,” Hiller explained. Hiller suggested that protecting McKenna’s confidence is part of the decision. “I just want to make sure he’s ready for that,” Hiller said. But, the decision becomes harder to justify as the Leafs season continues to slip away. Gavin McKenna’s Role Growing Despite Maple Leafs’ Struggles McKenna’s absence from overtime comes as Hiller experiments with his lineup in an effort to end Toronto’s prolonged slump. McKenna played alongside John Tavares on Thursday, skating 14:28 against the Kings, slightly above his season average of 13:57. Despite the lineup adjustments, Toronto squandered a three-goal lead against Los Angeles before falling in a shootout, extending its winless streak to eight games. Hiller has been tinkering without success, which brings more heat towards his decision to bench McKenna in overtime. Three-on-three hockey rewards speed, creativity and offensive instincts, all attributes that helped make McKenna such a highly regarded prospect. However, Hiller appears more concerned with ensuring his young forward is prepared for the defensive responsibilities and pressure that come with the extra period. item.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy won’t rule out Mason McCormick playoff return despite gruesome injury
item.description: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Steelers’ Mike McCarthy won’t rule out Mason McCormick playoff return despite gruesome injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . McCormick was placed on injured reserve , but there is a chance that he returns during the playoffs since there was no fracture in his ankle. Head coach Mike McCarthy was asked about a possible postseason return, and he said they’ve received positive updates, according to ESPN’s Brooke Pryor. “That would be great, but I think it’s so early. Everybody’s been very positive about all the information that’s been gathered to this point,” McCarthy said. But obviously prayers up for Mason. Just making sure we’re checking on the person, not really the player right now.” For now, it’ll be next man up for the Steelers, and it’ll be interesting to see how the offensive line holds up without one of their key pieces. The Steelers are currently 6-3 and are in second place in the AFC North. They’ve played well this season and have a chance of adding to their win total against the Philadelphia Eagles this week. item.title: SMU’s Texas-Sized Bet on Lacrosse
item.description: High school senior lacrosse standout Trystean Warburton grew up supporting his hometown school of SMU, often visiting the campus and rooting for the football program. But he never thought he could play college lacrosse there, let alone anywhere in his home state of Texas, which had zero NCAA Division I teams. But on Oct. 15, SMU announced the launch of the first D-I men’s lacrosse program, which will play in the highly competitive ACC beginning in 2028. Warburton, a four-star face-off specialist, flipped his Lehigh commitment almost immediately. “I loved [Lehigh]. I loved the coaching staff over there,” Warburton tells Front Office Sports . “But I always heard talks about the SMU program possibly being added to D-I, and I didn’t know if it was going to be really added into D-I during my years of playing. But I always dreamt of coming to SMU.” At a time when schools nationwide are considering cutting sports, SMU has found itself in the perfect position to start one—and hit the ground running. It has generous donors pouring millions into the program, already enabling it to poach an inaugural head coach with a championship pedigree; a state with an exploding interest in lacrosse, but a vacuum at the college level; and a new NCAA eligibility rule allowing it to build a roster that can compete for a D-I championship in Year 1. “Things just kind of came together,” SMU AD Damon Evans tells FOS. “Coupled with the fundraising, coupled with our founders, coupled with the interest [in Texas] … we just found that there was just so much coming together to allow us to get to the point where we are today.” Off to the Races The cash to stand up the Mustangs program flooded in quickly. On launch day, SMU announced it’d already secured a $15 million commitment. Evans says that war chest has swelled to $20 million to date, getting closer to the fundraising goal of $25 million. Chief among those donors are Gary and Sylvie Crum, whose fortune comes largely from investment management. The existing club lacrosse facility at SMU—infrastructure that has allowed the Mustangs to seamlessly step into varsity play—is named the Crum Lacrosse and Sports Field. (One of the main conference rooms in the USA Lacrosse headquarters in Maryland is also named after the family.) About two weeks after the launch, SMU announced it had hired Princeton offensive coordinator Jim Mitchell, the architect of the attack that propelled the Tigers to the 2026 national championship. In an October statement, Mitchell said: “The opportunity to build Texas’ first Division I men’s lacrosse program from the ground up, in a city like Dallas and a conference like the ACC, is something truly special. The expectation is to compete at the highest level, and I can’t wait to get started.” The NCAA’s new eligibility rule also “accelerated” the launch, Evans says. item.title: Naira depreciates to N1,472/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Naira today appreciated to N1,472 per dollar from N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market on Thursday. Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,394 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market rose to N1,394 per dollar from N1388 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N6 depreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N78 per dollar from N80 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM rose by 1.9 percent to $815.6 billion from $800.3 billion on Thursday. The post Naira depreciates to N1,472/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Shohei Ohtani signs lifetime deal with New Balance, plans changes to cleats
item.description: Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers will likely take him through the end of his playing career. Now, Ohtani has a career-long endorsement deal with his longtime sportswear provider to go along with it. Ohtani agreed to a new contract with New Balance that will last through the end of his baseball career, as he told GQ in a story published on Friday. It is believed to be the first such lifetime sponsorship deal for a baseball player, putting Ohtani alongside the likes of other superstar athletes such as LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo (with Nike) and Damian Lillard (with Adidas) to strike such a commitment. Los Angeles Dodgers Shohei Ohtani walks to the plate against the Atlanta Braves during the NLDS in Los Angeles, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. Wally Skalij for the CA Post “There’s a lot of trust,” Ohtani told GQ through an interpreter. “We’ve obviously built friendships, as well. They’ve been able to accommodate my requests, the things I’ve asked for, and, like I said, that takes the involvement of a lot of trust. That relationship has been very, very good and smooth. I had no reservations about extending our relationship.” Ohtani has been the face of New Balance’s baseball line since originally signing a long-term endorsement deal with the company in 2023. He has worn New Balance gloves and cleats during his rise as a four-time MVP and two-time World Series champion with the Dodgers and Angels. He has his own line of apparel with the company, complete with a custom logo. He has been prominently featured in New Balance television commercials and other marketing endeavors. Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) runs the bases on the field prior to a game against the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Saturday, September 19, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “I have a lot of direct input into the footwear and apparel,” Ohtani said. “That includes my style, which I like to keep simple, as well as performance-based requests, [like with my] spikes. Some years we make minor changes, and sometimes we’ll make a big change. They understand what I want.” The 32-year-old Ohtani is coming off a poor finish to his 2026 season, when injuries to his left knee and right arm prevented him from pitching in the second half of the campaign and contributed to an offensive slump down the stretch that lingered into the playoffs. Though he still finished second in National League MVP voting –– thanks to his 30 home runs, 81 RBIs and .889 OPS as a hitter, as well as an 8-2 record and 1.79 ERA in 14 starts as a pitcher –– the Dodgers have acknowledged they might need to adjust his two-way workload going into 2027. Ohtani and New Balance have been working on adjustments of their own this offseason, planning to reconfigure the design of his spikes after Ohtani “noted there’d been some moments of slippage on the heel of his landing foot when pitching,” according to GQ. “[Shohei] is very quick and clear wit

item.title: 49ers Pull Sneaky Move on Vikings Ahead of Mexico City Showdown
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers got a small leg up on the Minnesota Vikings heading into their Mexico City showdown Getty Jake Brendel of the San Francisco 49ers. Getty Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores has his unit playing among the best in the NFL Getty The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings are taking very different routes to Mexico City in Week 11. The 8-1 49ers flew straight from Dallas to Colorado Springs after Sunday’s 46-40 win over the Cowboys. They’re spending the week practicing at the Air Force Academy’s Falcon Stadium, which sits at 6,621 feet, to get used to the thin air. Meanwhile, the 7-2 Vikings are staying home in Eagan, Minnesota, and won’t fly south until Saturday. Estadio Banorte sits about 7,350 feet above sea level — more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. However, staying home might not have been the Vikings’ first choice. According to one 49ers player, San Francisco beat Minnesota to the punch. Vikings Tried to Book Air Force Academy After 49ers Getty San Francisco 49ers center Jake Brendel joked about the team booking the Air Force Academy before the Vikings 49ers center Jake Brendel spoke with NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco at the Air Force Academy this week and dropped an interesting nugget about how San Francisco landed the facility. “The team does a really good job of making sure we’re as prepared as possible — getting up at altitude and also just being able to have a week where you’re away from distractions and really just focus on the opponent that’s coming up,” Brendel said . “Someone told me that the Vikings called to get this place a week after we did. Luckily we got it instead of them.” It should be noted that Brendel’s account is secondhand. The Vikings maintain that the decision to stay home was allegedly made after extensive research. Still, this isn’t new territory for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who grew up in Denver. The 49ers spent a full week in Colorado before beating the Arizona Cardinals 38-10 in Mexico City in 2022. They also arrived in Melbourne a week early before beating the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 in Week 1. The Rams got there just 24 hours before kickoff. But Shanahan isn’t overselling the advantage either. “I think it helps,” Shanahan said. “It’s not make-or-break by any means, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better.” Why the Vikings Are Staying Home Before Mexico City Getty Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores has his unit playing among the best in the NFL Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the team’s altitude prep began “weeks ago,” and that the staff picked the brains of other organizations that deal with similar trips. “The people you talk to that do things like this a little bit more — whether it’s soccer teams, NBA teams, whatever it may be — we’re trying to gain all the information that we possibly can and then make a decision because we did not know,” O’Connell told reporters. item.title: Will MLB copy the Brewers? Their World Series title could reshape hitting philosophies
item.description: It's been less than a month since the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers accomplished something that for years felt inevitable and impossible: the first World Series title in franchise history. Surely, crumpled Miller Lite cans and loose strips of confetti from the parade still remain in the nooks and crannies of downtown Milwaukee. Hundreds of thousands of Wisconsinites had their love of baseball strengthened, reaffirmed, validated. The impact of that Brewers run could eventually stretch far beyond Badger State borders. Major League Baseball is a copycat league in a copycat world. Success fosters emulation, winning precipitates mimicry. The 2026 Brewers — the lineup in particular — were such a different beast from other recent champions that it's reasonable to expect that other teams might attempt to mirror various aspects of Milwaukee's strategic DNA. During the regular season, Milwaukee led baseball in several offensive categories, some traditionally considered conducive to scoring runs, others, not so much. The Brewers boasted the lowest chase rate in MLB at 26.8% and, accordingly, the highest walk rate (10.6%). That's an obvious recipe for success, a tale as old as time, or at least the Moneyball A's. See pitches, draw walks, be patient, get ahead in counts and you'll force pitchers to feed you more juicy pitches to hit. Milwaukee was also prolific at producing batted balls to the opposite field (league-leading 29.4%) and on the ground (48.1%). They ranked dead last in MLB in "pull air percentage" at 12.4%. The Chicago Cubs, the only club to score more runs than Milwaukee in 2026, led all of baseball in pull air percentage with a 21.5% mark. Milwaukee bulldozed its way to the title that included an NLCS sweep and a gentleman's sweep in the World Series. Erick W. Rasco via Getty Images It's worth noting that over the last decade, the league has experienced a dramatic increase in pull air percentage, from 14.9 in 2015 to 18.4 in 2026. That's in line with contemporary hitting philosophy. Power (and the corresponding runs and riches) comes in the air. For most players, that slug is easier to come by to the pull side. From Justin Turner to pre-falloff Chris Davis to Cal Raleigh to Kyle Schwarber to Isaac Paredes, we've seen time and time again that learning to pull the baseball with authority leads to good results. The Brewers, to a certain extent, bucked that trend and did so proudly. Accolades and earnings usually come via power production. Milwaukee's selfless offensive approach prioritized the whole over the individual. But will the Brewers' success motivate any noticeable shift in hitting philosophy? Can we expect more back-side grounders whenever the sport resumes in 2027? It's complicated. ‘We're certainly paying attention’ to what the Brewers are doing’ "You know, this comes up anytime anybody wins—people look at the way they won and say, 'This is the new way,'" St. Louis Cardinals president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom told Yahoo Sports at the

item.title: Seahawks’ $9.9 Million Cap Move Includes Darnold, Raises Free-Agent Signing Possibility
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks looks on against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Quarterback Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks takes the field prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks looks on during the first quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have suddenly made nearly $10 million available under the salary cap. The timing raises a question about what general manager John Schneider might have planned. Seattle restructured the contracts of quarterback Sam Darnold, safety Julian Love and linebacker Ernest Jones IV, according to Spotrac’s November 20 reports. The three moves created approximately $9.87 million in 2026 cap space. With the Seahawks heading into their bye week at 6-4, the sudden financial flexibility could hint at a potential free-agent addition. Seattle hasn’t announced plans to pursue a specific player, however. Seahawks Restructure Three Major Contracts Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – NOVEMBER 02: Quarterback Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks takes the field prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) The Seahawks made their largest adjustment to Darnold’s contract. According to Spotrac , Seattle converted $5.5 million of the quarterback’s salary into a signing bonus and added another void year. That move freed $4.4 million in cap space for 2026. Darnold’s cap hit now stands at $33.5 million this season, with a projected $43 million charge in 2027. The Seahawks made similar adjustments to two defensive starters. Seattle converted $3.5 million of Love’s salary into a signing bonus, adding three void years and creating $2.8 million in space. His 2026 cap hit now stands at $10 million, followed by $15.9 million in 2027. The Seahawks also restructured Jones’ contract , converting $3.34 million into a signing bonus and adding three void years. That freed another $2.67 million. Together, the adjustments provide Seattle with much more room to operate during the final stretch of the regular season. item.title: ‘The NFL was unaware’: NFL reportedly didn’t have full story on Puka Nacua’s injury before suspension
item.description: Sep 11, 2026; Melbourne, AUS; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) practices before the game at Melbourne Cricket Ground. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is having a rough week. On Thursday, the NFL announced that Nacua would be suspended for three games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy The news seemed like a break at first, as Nacua was placed on Injured Reserve on Nov. 12th with a posterior cruciate ligament/MCL sprain and turf toe, which mandates that he miss at least four games, covering the length of his suspension. However, on Friday, Rams head coach Sean McVay updated his star wide receiver’s situation, and it sounds like Nacua’s season may be over. “Rams star WR Puka Nacua will undergo MCL surgery and is likely going to miss the rest of the season,” The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported on X. Rams star WR Puka Nacua will undergo MCL surgery and is likely going to miss the rest of the season. He’ll be out “a couple months,” per Sean McVay. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) November 20, 2026 ESPN’s Adam Schefter provided an update to the story shortly after news broke, reporting that Nacua had already undergone surgery on his knee when the league punished him. “The NFL was unaware that Rams WR Puka Nacua had undergone knee surgery Tuesday when it suspended him for three games Wednesday, per source,” the insider posted on X. Nacua will now turn his focus to rehab, but will have to remain on his best behavior off the field as he works his way back. After levying a three-game suspension, the NFL made it clear that any further conduct violations, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, would result in further and severe punishment, including banishment from the league. The post ‘The NFL was unaware’: NFL reportedly didn’t have full story on Puka Nacua’s injury before suspension appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Rob Manfred says no compromise on salary cap with MLBPA + first big trade of the offseason
item.description: Subscribe to Baseball Bar-B-Cast Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube As the offseason progresses in its early infancy, the elephant in the room, known as the expiring CBA, is only going to get bigger. Commissioner Rob Manfred spoke at the owners' meetings this past week and gave his thoughts on not compromising on the possibility of a salary cap, signaling how much of a struggle this situation could become between the league and players. On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast, Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman talk about the comments made by the commissioner and try to distinguish what they mean for negotiations with the players and why using the fans as a major part of the league's argument is an interesting strategy. They also discuss his striking comments regarding working through the Thanksgiving holiday and why this is only the beginning of the public posturing. Later in the show, Jake and Jordan go around the league and highlight two notable trades that went down, including the Seattle Mariners acquiring Maikel Garcia from the Kansas City Royals and the Colorado Rockies trading for Luis Castillo and Davis Martin from the Chicago White Sox. They then talk about Sonny Gray returning to the Minnesota Twins and the New York Mets and New York Yankees bolstering their bullpens. item.title: Report – Manchester City star agrees to Juventus move
item.description: Report – Manchester City star agrees to Juventus move Juventus continue to pursue a new left back and are hoping to strengthen that position during the January transfer window. Rayan Ait-Nouri has emerged as one of their main targets as they look to bring in a player who can improve their options in that area of the pitch. The defender has struggled to secure regular playing time at Manchester City since the start of this season, raising questions about his future at the Premier League club. City could be open to allowing him to leave, particularly if an opportunity arises to move him on during the next transfer window. Juventus regard Ait-Nouri as one of the best players available for the position and have continued working towards bringing him to their squad. The Italian side have been looking to strengthen at left back for some time and believe the City defender could be an excellent addition. Ait-Nouri open to Juventus move Ait-Nouri has spent considerable time in the Premier League and is widely regarded as a quality defender. However, his situation at City has become increasingly difficult because of the competition for places, limiting his opportunities to demonstrate his abilities. According to Tuttojuve , the defender has now agreed to the possibility of joining Juventus as he looks for a change of scenery. He reportedly believes that his lack of playing time at City means his talents are not being used sufficiently and is therefore open to continuing his career in Italy. The opportunity to work under Luciano Spalletti could also appeal to the defender, particularly if he is offered more regular involvement in the team. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) January transfer could be on the cards Juventus have been trying to strengthen their left-back position since last summer, making Ait-Nouri an attractive option as they prepare for the January window. His reported willingness to join Juve could make negotiations easier, although an agreement between the clubs would still be required to complete the transfer. For Juventus, securing a player with Premier League experience would represent a significant addition to their defensive options. Meanwhile, Ait-Nouri could benefit from a fresh challenge and the opportunity to play more regularly. With January approaching, the possibility of a move appears increasingly realistic if Juventus can reach an agreement with Manchester City.

That’s especially true this year, as rising hardware prices have made MacBooks and other Apple devices even more expensive. Fortunately, Black Friday offers a chance to save, especially since great deals are already available on a wide range of Apple devices. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , which have dropped to new lows. Most of the discounts below are promoted as Black Friday deals, but we’ve also included a few that aren’t technically part of the shopping event but have “coincidentally” dropped in price in the last week or so. Black Friday isn’t until November 27th, however, so some prices could fall further in the coming days. Apple is also kicking off its own Black Friday shopping event that day, offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases. That said, if you don’t want to wait, we think the deals below are already worth taking advantage of. Earbud and headphone deals AirPods Pro 3 The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $179 at Amazon $249 $179 at Walmart $249 $179.99 at Best Buy Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $179.95 at Amazon $249 $179.95 at Walmart $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon , which is $19 shy of their best price to date ( Best Buy and Target also have them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review . Beats Studio Pro The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort.
