item.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
item.description: Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents which worked autonomously to find a zero-day in an open source application and then abuse the flaw to break into university networks, gaining full control of a server, according to Amazon CISO CJ Moses. The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance . In this case, the agents found and exploited a zero-day MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon notified the project's maintainers of the vulnerability, and they released a fix and a security advisory . On September 10, Amazon's Threat Intelligence Team found a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn that provided visibility into the campaign targeting universities in East Asia, outside Mainland China, Moses said in a Friday report shared with The Register . The campaign occurred over a period of 48 hours beginning on September 8, and the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese, with timestamps in executed scripts configured to China Standard Time. Before the AI agents found and exploited the zero day, however, they tried to break into another university’s Redis server over about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions, including abusing Redis's replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory. None of these were successful, and when those actions failed, the agents also attempted a Log4Shell injection against a different service, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack against a vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance, and several credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and other tools. Meanwhile, a separate operation running for more than 6 hours targeted a university GPU server with another credential-spray attack, compiling a list of 80 real user names found across the school’s public websites, academic papers and other documents. "Neither operation succeeded, yet together they show that the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction," Moses wrote. Then the AI agents found the zero-day path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label, and this time they were able to gain access to the server. "The agents identified the application's framework, mapped its API endpoints, and found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter," Moses wrote. They tested that parameter for path traversal, and the parameter was vulnerable. In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application’s API to arbitrarily writing files on the server." Later, the agents abused the same flaw to execute a Python reverse shell running as root. In another session, after the agents discovered the zero-day, the human operator provided them with a proxy that tunneled into a second university network, and connected to a server running the same vulnerable

item.description: Denmark’s foreign minister on Friday said Moscow’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Russia was suspected of being behind an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper. “We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark” within seven days, Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference. “We are saying this very clearly: we have exposed you”, he said. He also added Denmark was mulling suspending Schengen visas to Russians. “We have launched work at the European level to further tighten the rules governing access of Russian nationals to Europe,” he said. “We are now stepping up our efforts — towards a halt to all non-essential visas”. “The strongest response Denmark can give is not to waver and to support Ukraine. And we fully intend to continue” supporting Ukraine, he said. The announcements came after Danish intelligence said it suspected Russia of planning the assassination of a Ukrainian rapper during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb with the help of a Danish criminal gang. item.title: 2027 Election: ‘What President Tinubu is thinking about’
item.description: …targets 18/18 victory for APC in Cross River By Ike Uchechukwu – CALABAR Minister of State for Industry, Sen. John Owan-Enoh, says President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than winning the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened Tinubu’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the situation as temporary sacrifices necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the administration’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further said inflation had declined to about 14 per cent and expressed optimism that it would continue falling towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying the state needed to remain influential in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in 2027. He recalled that Tinubu won seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas in the 2023 presidential election. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the Jan. 16, 2027 election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come Jan. 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: ‘What President Tinubu is thinking about’ appeared first on V

item.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
item.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. Physical or cyberattacks against ground sites and other terrestrial infrastructure supporting space operations can also threaten satellite services. item.title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.” Researchers ask for review The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. Kudinov said it has not been sufficiently peer reviewed, and the project’s GitHub repository warns that the documents may contain errors and should not be the sole basis for deploy

item.title: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
item.description: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) has officially advised consumers against buying AI-powered smart glasses after safety tests revealed concerning behaviors beyond their controversial recording capabilities. The AP recently tested six different models of smart glasses and found glaring issues, including a willingness to display dating advice to an adult glasses-wearer who expressed an interest in a minor. In another case involving a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) simulation, testers noted that one pair of glasses informed the wearer that emergency services had been called and were scheduled to arrive at the scene, despite no one having made the call. Some glasses did not properly process safety warnings on children’s toys, others made mistakes when reading medication leaflets, and some misinterpreted warnings for extreme weather events. The AP did not specify the models it tested, saying only that they tested six models ranging from under €100 ($110) to over €500 ($550), including two that "were extensively tested in simulated real-life situations where human safety played a key role." A spokesperson also declined to match any specific behavior to a model by price point (minor dating advice linked to a €354 pair of glasses, for example), adding that the research was intended to highlight the risks of AI glasses in a broader sense. "Glasses that film you unnoticed are already concerning. Glasses that also give you incorrect advice when someone's life is at stake go a step too far," said Monique Verdier, vice chair at the AP. "AI offers many opportunities, but we must be able to trust that technology. With the camera glasses examined, that trust cannot currently be justified." The warning issued this week follows the regulator's previous work on smart glasses. The AP reminded the public in September that everyone has the right to privacy and encouraged organizations to ban them where necessary. The same warning mentioned the potential risks regarding data processing under the GDPR, as well as those related to the training of AI. The AP doubled down on these earlier criticisms, saying the latest tests showed that the AI functions rely on processing data using servers mostly located outside of the European Union. Relatedly, it found that users were not given sufficient information about how the AI was processing the data they captured. On a cybersecurity note, the tests threw up a range of issues, including the ability for people nearby the glasses-wearer to connect to the device without permission, view recordings, and in some cases operate the camera. Further, the regulator echoed the pre-existing concerns about smart specs - those that helped give them their colloquial name “pervert glasses.” Its tests found that with "virtually all of the camera glasses examined," the recording lights that are supposed to clearly show when a user is recording were dim and easily coverable. item.title: Poland and allies say Russian missile a ‘provocation’ from Moscow
item.description: Warsaw and its allies said Friday that a Russian missile landing in Poland was a “provocation” from Moscow as thousands of European troops were holding exercises nearby. Poland said two Russian missiles hit its territory early on Friday, landing in southeastern Poland as drills were due to take place. Nobody was hurt, Poland said. Authorities said one Kh-101 missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec. A second missile is suspected to have hit another location and a jet-powered drone a third. The projectiles crossed into the NATO country as Russia pounded neighbouring Ukraine and thousands of European troops were holding unprecedented army drills in southeastern Poland. Several European defence ministers were in Poland for the drills. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said everything pointed to the fact that these were not accidental stray missiles. “Three Russian objects violated Polish airspace. They fell on Polish land. One exploded. There is no destruction, no casualties,” he said, adding: “This is not just my opinion but of our foreign partners and NATO: this does not look like a coincidence.” He said he believed the incident was linked to the European drills. “We are dealing with an intentional provocation,” he added. He said the objects “fell close” to where “armies of the Coalition of the Willing” were training in Nowa Deba, southeastern Poland. “Coalition of the Willing” refers to a group of Ukraine’s European backers who are prepared to send peacekeeping troops to the country. Nowy Lipowiec, where the first missile fell, is a 1.5-hour drive from where the drills are taking place. Just a day before the incident, US media outlet Fox News quoted Donald Trump as saying Russian leader Vladimir Putin “has been landing drones in Poland, and a couple of little missiles, by mistake”. Tusk said on Friday that Poland would give the United States access to the missile debris. “I don’t always agree with the interpretation of the US side on these incidents. We are cooperating with the Americans. They have access to the places, to the debris of the objects.” The Kremlin has not yet commented. The missiles flew in as Russian strikes killed at least eight people in Ukraine, a day after Putin met with Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. ‘Putin seeks confrontation’ UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the “incursion into Polish airspace is utterly unacceptable”, while the EU said it stood in “full solidarity” with the Poles. Germany said the incident was “yet another example of Russia’s ongoing provocations” and that “rather than showing a willingness to negotiate, Putin… continues to seek confrontation”. The French presidency called it a “serious incident”. item.title: Akpabio charges APC support groups against electoral violence
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio has urged support groups and members of the All Progressives Congress, APC, not to allow themselves to be provoked to carry out attacks or retaliate against members of the opposition as the party was better positioned to win in a free and fair election. Senator Akpabio gave the charge in Abuja on Friday at the inauguration of “Tinubu Again Movement” a grassroots mobilization movement, convened by the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Matawalle, aimed at securing more than 20 million votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027. In a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media/Communication to the President of the Senate, Anietie Ekong, Akpabio urged the APC members and supporters not to be distracted by the antics of the opposition parties who aimed to attract sympathy by inciting violence in the run up to the election. The President of the Senate said: “Please be careful. Don’t allow them to provoke you to violence. Because they know they are losing, they will sponsor some misguided youths to throw stones at you. If they throw stones at you, your target is to garner votes and defeat them. “By January 16, 2027, they will know the difference between stones and votes. When you are certain of winning you don’t deploy stones and violence as your weapons but you persuade them with the monumental achievement of the APC administration.” Akpabio charged the members of Tinubu Again Movement to carry the message of the Renewed Hope administration to their various polling units, wards and local government areas to sensitize the populace on the achievement of the administration of President Tinubu. Akpabio who was the Chairman at the inauguration, reeled out some of the achievements of the administration to include, the Lagos – Calabar coastal highway, the Sokoto – Badagry highway, and other road infrastructure across the States. He said the economy of the country had almost collapsed before the advent of rhe Tinubu administration and commended the administration for the courageous removal of fuel subsidy which he said had made more funds available to States and Local Governments to execute projects without resorting to borrowing. According to him, the introduction of the Students Loan Fund had made it possible for indigent students to access education just as the tax reforms had recaliberated the economy, adding, “Today the States are benefitting from the economic reforms. Many Governors are executing projects without borrowing a dime because of the ingenuity of one man, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “So when you go out there to talk about how President Tinubu must be returned to office with over 20 million votes, say it with boldness because this President had stabilized and grown the economy and the indices are there for all to see!” Akpabio commended Dr Matawalle for the initiative in convening the Tinubu Again Movement and urged other political appointees to em

item.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike, even as bitcoin broke below $60,000 for the first time since July and stocks sank on bets that the Fed will keep tightening into a selloff. Bessent told CNBC he would encourage the Fed not to embrace a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He cited the energy supply shock and a drop in crude prices as reasons for the central bank to hold back. Bessent says the Fed should look forward He argued that one governor now backing a 50 basis point hike had wanted a similar cut within the last year. Bessent said it “seems somewhat peripatetic” to want the bigger increase only 11 or 12 months later. He did not name the governor. “I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards,” Bessent said. The comments came two days after Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC a half-point hike is probably necessary in December and that the central bank may need to “shock people.” Waller said inflation is “headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out.” Fed officials split on how far to go Waller is not alone. Minutes of the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, and two floated a larger one. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also declined to rule out a bigger move on Thursday. “We’ve now had multiple months in a row of borderline disturbingly high inflation rates with little progress in the sectors where we would expect to be seeing some progress,” Goolsbee told reporters. “So everything’s always on the table.” Not everyone wants to go bigger. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action.” St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem has suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years and held them steady in October. Inflation has stayed hot since the Iran strikes pushed up energy prices earlier this year. Citi and traders still see a quarter-point hike Citi still expects a quarter-point increase in December. Global chief economist Nathan Sheets said Thursday he does not see a need for 50 basis points despite persistent inflation. In a note Friday, the bank wrote that “Fed officials will consequently have little appetite to hike into an equity sell-off.” Citi expects the Fed to hold after December and begin cutting later in 2027. Traders agree on the next step: the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point hike, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points to 4.95% as investors bought bonds. Stocks fell for another day. The Nasdaq Composite dropped more than 2% in morning trading, and the VIX volatility index topped 30 , its highest level since March. item.title: Russia pummels Ukraine, missile hits Poland, after Putin threat
item.description: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of “provocation” after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country. Russia’s Vladimir Putin had vowed a “painful” response to Kyiv’s strikes on Moscow’s Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China’s Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow’s largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he said was Russian “terror”. Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin’s attempts to “redraw the world” with Xi and Trump had been a “failure”. In China, Putin said he “shared responsibility” for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a “declaration toward peace” that made no mention of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine. AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv’s metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents. Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment. “It’s painful to have to stop our child from living,” she told AFP. Two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said. Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired. Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city. France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying “Russia will have to answer for its actions there”. Poland decries ‘provocation’ In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations. Warsaw said no-one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate. “The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland,” Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw. Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland. “Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence,” Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO “straight away”. Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident. Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine. Bridge retaliation Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet. item.title: Valve says it might have to raise the price of supply-limited Steam Machines
item.description: When the Steam Machine first started shipping in June , Valve said it was producing fewer units at a higher price than initially planned because it couldn't secure supplies of scarce RAM and storage components at a reasonable cost. Now, as the last of the initial batch of Steam Machine reservations are finally being fulfilled, Valve says those supply and cost issues will continue into the foreseeable future and may even require a price change. "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels," Valve wrote in a blog post on Thursday . "As a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained." If Valve does have to raise the price of the Steam Machine, it will be in good company. All three major console manufacturers instituted historically atypical price increases in 2025 , with additional price hikes happening this year. Read full article Comments

item.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
item.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. But it would like governments to step in, of course, by tracking board and material lead times

item.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. JUST IN: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for the first time since June. BTC is now less than 4% away from a new cycle low pic.twitter.com/GSZkbGdzZz — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 20, 2026 ETF outflows and liquidations Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week. Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them. The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday. Crypto stocks fall harder than bitcoin price Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight

item.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada

You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. item.title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military. Read Also: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits. Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military. “That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military. Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported. “No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added. The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons. The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes. In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors. He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities. The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country. item.title: Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A tragedy struck the riverine enclave of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area on Friday, as a cargo boat conveying over 300 passengers capsized, leaving many feared dead. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly en route to Ukubie community from Anyama Ijaw, when the incident occurred at 12 noon. According to preliminary reports, the boat, which was heavily overloaded with passengers traveling for a burial ceremony, went down in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts indicate that the tragedy might have been averted. It was learned that some passengers had suggested the boat stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel, but the advice was allegedly ignored. The boat reportedly capsized shortly after departing the community. While the actual casualty figure remains unconfirmed, fears are mounting that the death toll could be substantial given the number of persons on board. Mr. Ipigansi Igoniba, Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but stated that information regarding the disaster was still hazy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations are currently underway, though independent confirmation of the number of survivors or fatalities is yet to be established. The incident has cast a pall of mourning over the community, highlighting once again the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe travel on the state’s waterways. Vanguard News The post Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis
item.description: The Riemann hypothesis describes a pattern within the prime numbers ROBERT BROOK/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY/Alamy A mathematician at AI company Anthropic claims to have discovered, and verified with formalisation, a proof of the Riemann hypothesis – one of the most infamous and thorny problems in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Read more OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published a statement today claiming to have solved the problem with the aid of Anthropic’s Claude AI. Advertisement “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” writes Alpöge. “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” In August, Anthropic announced previous work on the Riemann hypothesis , but that stopped short of a full proof. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. Instead, Alpöge has released a version of the proof written in Lean, a computer code mathematicians use to mechanically verify proofs as a series of logical steps in a process called formalisation. This process is so thorough that if a theorem comes through intact, meaning that the code compiles, it is considered to have been proved correct beyond all reasonable doubt. However, the process isn’t without vulnerabilities, and the code and mathematics will need to be thoroughly checked by humans. “Let’s see if it compiles first,” says Kevin Buzzard at Imperial College London, reacting to the news. “Might be a while before we find the relevant experts who are able to tell us the thrust of the argument, assuming it’s all true, of course, which it probably will be because of course Alpöge will have [a] huge amount of egg on [his] face if the Lean code doesn’t compile or is deficient in some way.” A golden age of maths is dawning and mathematicians are freaking out Mathematicians are stunned at the progress AI is making in solving advanced problems, leaving some questioning whether there will still be room for humans Alpöge says the proof may also help solve the generalised Riemann hypothesis (GRH), which widens out the concept to different properties of prime numbers, and could expand our understanding of a broader family of mathematical structures. “There are numerous results that are conditional on the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and now

item.title: 'Critical' 1970s-era Fujitsu UK police system could remain unsupported for three years
item.description: The UK's Home Office faces running the Police National Computer (PNC) without vendor support for three years or more as it misses another deadline to decommission the ageing crime-fighting system first introduced in 1974. The PNC was first launched in 1974, when Tom Baker began his iconic role playing Doctor Who, and has seen the tenure of 26 UK Home Secretaries, surviving multiple efforts to replace it. A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." We understand that PNC support refers to the Fujitsu support contract for the mainframe, which is housed in north London. Support for the Software AG database on the mainframe OS (BS2000) ran out at the end of 2024. So the database holding the crucial police data remains out of standard support and potentially will stay that way until 2027. The decommissioning date for the PNC had already been pushed back by the need to delay and "reset" the LEDS in 2020. The Home Office launched its successor, National Law Enforcement Data Service, in 2016, and planned to finish the new system by 2020 at a cost of £671 million. The Home Office told The Register this week that it needed more time, and it aimed to begin decommissioning the system from March 2027, raising questions over how it would be supported. A Home Office spokesperson said: "We are modernizing policing systems to adapt to evolving challenges, including rolling out the LEDS to replace the Police National Computer. "While LEDS is already operational, we are continuing to run the legacy Police National Computer system to support the operational needs of all UK police," they said. Officials said the PNC would remain available throughout the transition and would only be disconnected when police forces have confirmed that they no longer need it. Earlier this month, in a written response in the House of Lords, Lord Hanson of Flint, a junior minister, said the PNC might be required until early 2028. Some LEDS services were already live and the program was "targeting completion of the remaining development, adoption and readiness activity in early 2027 as we prepare for our final stages for LEDS deployment before retiring the PNC," he said. "Once the transition of all police users to the LEDS has been completed and policing has confirmed that the PNC is no longer required, the system will be disconnected and decommissioned. The decommissioning process is expected to take place between late 2027 and early 2028," he said . According to the National Audit Office (NAO), the PNC is the most important national policing information system in the UK. It serves front-line officers from all 45 local police forces, as well as by 127 other organisations that need to access its data. In 20

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: ISS astronauts look down on the snow-capped Himalayas | Space photo of the day for Nov. 20, 2026
item.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.

item.title: US will soon announce root cause behind FAA nationwide ground stop
item.description: The US government will announce soon the root cause of the router outage that led to the third-ever nationwide ground stop issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration. But questions remain about whether the FAA's effort to modernize the national airspace system is being done with all the proper risk assessments and adequate agency oversight of the private contractors involved. The nationwide ground stop blocked flight departures and impacted more than 1 million passengers across the United States for more than four hours on Friday, November 13. More than 12,000 flights were canceled on that day alone, with the number rising to more than 20,000 over the weekend as stranded travelers scrambled to find accommodations or alternative transportation. Some international flights were allowed to depart prior to the broader resumption of air traffic. Nearly one week later, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told news reporters that government investigators are “very close” to figuring out the root cause of the nationwide ground stop, according to CNN . Bedford also said that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to announce the findings at a news conference as soon as Friday, November 20. Read full article Comments

item.title: Lagos Hosts 2026 International Theatre Festival, Featuring Local and International Productions
item.description: The third edition of the Lagos International Theatre Festival (LITF) has concluded successfully, attracting over 20,000 attendees from November 9 to 15, 2026. Featuring more than 25 productions, international performances from Kenya, Brazil, Norway and Canada, high-profile diplomatic engagements and a spectacular Opening Night Gala, the festival reinforced its growing position as an important platform for showcasing Nigerian creativity and connecting global theatre communities. The impressive turnout, diversity of productions and international participation demonstrated the growing appetite for live theatre and the potential of cultural platforms to stimulate creative enterprise, encourage international collaboration and strengthen Nigeria’s global cultural presence. A Vision For Global Recognition Speaking on the success of the festival, Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists. Welcoming over 20,000 attendees, presenting more than 25 productions and bringing international performers from four countries to Lagos is a powerful affirmation of this vision. Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence. The Stage Is Everywhere, and Africa must claim its rightful place on that stage.” A Week Of Culture And Collaboration The festival opened on November 9 with Theatre Meets Food at Kaly Restaurant, featuring celebrated chef Hilda Baci in a unique fusion of culinary artistry and live performance. The week also featured diplomatic and cultural engagements hosted by the United States Consul General in Lagos and the British Embassy, alongside a networking reception organised by the British Council for festival directors and participating production companies. These engagements highlighted the importance of international partnerships and cultural diplomacy in advancing Nigeria’s creative industry. A Celebration Of Excellence A major highlight was the Opening Night Gala, held on November 13 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, which welcomed over 1,000 guests, including the Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu ; the Chargé d’Affaires of the US Mission in Nigeria; the US Consul General; the British Deputy High Commissioner; the Consul General of Brazil; the Consul General of South Africa, the Ambassador of the Republic of Korea; alongside other members of the diplomatic corps, heads of institutions, government representatives, international delegates and leading figures in the creative industry. item.title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases. The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29. Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period. “Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy. Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73. Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent. Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days. The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest. Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars. A push for a de minimis bitcoin exemption Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said. A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%. Consumers pointed to friction, too. item.title: MultiChoice cuts entry-level DStv, GOtv subscriptions to ₦6,000
item.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. item.title: COP31 wrapping up in Turkey: Climate deal elusive as fossil fuels go unmentioned
item.description: The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations. The talks come with a series of stark reminders of the urgency of climate action, from heatwaves in Europe and devastating floods in Nepal, while a record-breaking El Nino supercharges temperatures. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

item.title: US, Russia and China look set to block ban on autonomous weapons
item.description: More than 70 countries are ready to begin negotiations on prohibiting lethal autonomous weapons, but large militarised nations are expected to obstruct efforts to agree a ban

item.title: Burnham hails 'landmark' EU-UK deal as 'good day' for Britain, Europe
item.description: Britain and the European Union agreed deals on trade, carbon emissions and youth movement on Friday, and pledged to rebuild ties with an “ambitious and dynamic” post-Brexit relationship. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap checks on the trade in plant and animal products, link their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other's countries for up to three years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Russia pummels Ukraine with massive strikes, missile hits Poland
item.description: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least six people were killed in the capital, and neighbouring Poland reporting two Russian missiles likely landed in the south-east corner of the NATO country, accusing Moscow of a "provocation." Hours earlier, Russia's Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: Berrada on Carrick, Poch, defending club leadership and transfers
item.description: In a turbulent time at Manchester United, chief executive Omar Berrada has sat down exclusively with Sky Sports about United's start to the season, the decision to change head coach and facing fan criticism about the club's leadership.

item.title: 'GTA VI': When the biggest-ever entertainment release becomes the biggest headline
item.description: This week FRANCE 24's media show "Scoop" looks at how the press covered the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI". Pre-orders and first-day sales totalled more than $2.3 billion. What does the game and the franchise's success mean for the future of entertainment? Our guest is Margaret Wallace, a video game developer and an associate professor of the practice of media innovation at Boston University.

item.title: France probes suspected leak of confidential information to Le Pen's party
item.description: French authorities are investigating whether a former senior official at the Interior Ministry leaked confidential information about judicial investigations into far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally, adding to the party's legal woes ahead of a presidential election next year in which Le Pen is the current frontrunner.

item.title: A decade after Brexit, do Britons regret leaving the EU?
item.description: Britain and the European Union went through a bitter divorce, then slowly began trying to rebuild their relationship. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met the EU's top officials in Brussels on Friday for a summit he has described as a step towards undoing a decade of damage caused by the 2016 vote to leave the bloc. But how do the British public feel about closer ties with the EU – and, potentially, rejoining it?

item.title: Microsoft's last non-security preview of 2026 packs a punch
item.description: Microsoft has delivered its final scheduled non-security preview update of 2026 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, with an updated Windows Search experience and a brighter Windows Hello for users who prefer darker rooms. The optional KB5132057 update arrived on November 19, after this month's Patch Tuesday. Microsoft is skipping December's non-security preview because of reduced holiday operations, though that doesn't cancel the monthly security release. This last preview is quite a doozy. The big-ticket item is the "new Windows Search Experience." We saw a preview of this last month, and Microsoft has gone well beyond the "just make it work" request of many Windows users. Results appear faster with less clutter, the tool uses memory better, and files can be previewed directly in Windows Search. We're less convinced by inline actions, which let users perform common tasks directly through Windows Search without opening Settings. In our testing, "turn on dark mode" worked, but "switch on dark mode" did not, thus highlighting the limitations of the tool. In addition, we remain unconvinced that Windows Search is the place to run actions. That said, anything that makes Windows Search less of a punchline for unkind jokes about performance and accuracy is welcome, as are other features, including an optional screen-brightening feature for Windows Hello facial recognition in dim rooms, and the PowerToys-esque Run dialog, which users can enable in Settings. While some of the new features won't be enabled immediately, Microsoft has included fixes that will be available right away. One addresses an issue where Windows Fax and Scan could fail to connect to a fax server. Handy for those occasions when email falls over into a heap . There are also fixes for Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC activation failures and the misleading "Something went wrong" message shown on Android devices during cross-device passkey authentication. At the time of writing, Microsoft still lists the problem as something for which "we are working on a resolution to be released in a future Windows update." Sadly, not everything has been pushed off the naughty step. SQL Server queries using OLE DB providers can still leave connections to external databases open after they've finished. Microsoft is working on that one and "will provide an update in an upcoming release." ®

item.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. He said misinformation surrounding Ebola outbreaks in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo similarly fuelled distrust of health workers and undermined disease-control interventions. “These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability but also human lives,” he warned. Okonkwo maintained that the emergence of AI-generated content had made information verification more urgent, particularly as digital platforms increasingly allowed individuals to publish and

item.title: Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday. The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater. The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price. What the realized price measures Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market. The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost. The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report. “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.” Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported . U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day. The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week. Leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total. CoinShares sees range trading through 2027 CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.
